title: The postponed match at Bell Yard School
public_context: A fictional league secretary writes a post-match report concerning a club fixture. The account uses the familiar setting of a local competition and its sporting records, in the secretary's own prose rather than as a season table. The people, clubs, and event are invented.
source_title: Fixtures secretary's report on Latchford Athletic and Moss Vale
source_text:
Latchford Athletic and Moss Vale were due to meet at Latchford on 12 September. A water-main break left standing water across the center of the ground, and the municipal inspector closed the pitch before either side began warm-ups. No kickoff took place that afternoon. I crossed the date from the fixture sheet and left the points column empty; the league does not award points for a match that never starts.

The clubs proposed a Wednesday evening replay, but the school ground normally used by Moss Vale had a parents' meeting that night. They agreed to play at Bell Yard School instead, with Latchford listed as the home side and Moss Vale using the visitors' changing room. The league kept the original referee, who had already been assigned to the fixture, and moved the date to 29 September. Both club secretaries signed the amendment before it went on the notice board.

Two days before the replay, Latchford asked to name a fourth substitute because one registered player could not leave work in time for the new weekday slot. The competition committee declined the request: the ordinary three-substitute rule applied to rearranged fixtures as well. Latchford named a replacement from its registered list, and the team sheet was accepted at the school gate. Moss Vale arrived on the first bus from the old ground and had time to warm up on the far touchline.

Moss Vale scored before the interval, and Latchford equalized from a corner soon after the teams changed ends. In the final minutes, Latchford's forward sent the ball across the line from the right side. The assistant referee kept the flag down, and the referee awarded the goal; the signed card records a 2–1 finish to Latchford. Moss Vale's captain submitted a written objection about whether the ball had crossed the boundary before the pass. I stapled the note to the card and sent both to the competition committee.

The school caretaker returned the corner flags on Thursday and kept the waterlogged September fixture sheet in a clear sleeve. The replacement card remains in the league book beside the signed date amendment.
